# Beta 1.0.3 · October 2026

## New things you can do
- Agents can use your Mac whatever its screen shape, including MacBooks with the notch and wide monitors.
- Your server installs its own updates when nothing is running, so it keeps up with the app. The owner can turn this off in Settings › Updates.
- When the server is behind the app, the app says so and offers one button to update it.
- You can delete an agent: right-click it in the sidebar, or use the chat's menu. For 30 days you can bring it back, chats and all, from Settings › Agents.
- The same menus open that agent's own settings.
- Settings › Agents has a card for your Claude accounts: add one, put them in order, and choose whether agents move to the next one when one runs out.
- In Approvals, you can ask for a change to a suggested routine instead of only approving or declining it.
- Removing a package now stops what it runs, such as its routines and reading mail. Deleting its data and forgetting its sign-ins are separate boxes, left unticked.
- Agents check a paper before they cite it: that it exists, that the details match, whether it was retracted, and where a free copy is.

## Things that read differently
- The server is called the server everywhere, in every message and menu, with no older name left over.
- The About panels in both apps give the version by its Beta name.

## Things that behave better
- The red button hides the window and the app keeps running; click its Dock icon to bring it back.
- The server app can leave the Dock (Show in Dock, in its window), and every menu in its menu bar icon opens the window.
- In a chat, the agent's reasoning starts folded while it thinks.
- Deadline alerts warn you two days ahead instead of one.
- Guests stay connected when the server moves to a new address, and pairing says whether you joined as owner or guest.
- Messages with emoji or Cyrillic arrive intact, and memory search finds Cyrillic and accented words.
- Sending from one chat pane no longer pulls focus from another.
- A chat no longer jumps when a picture in it finishes loading.
- With Reduce motion on, the thinking dots and the saving pulse stay still.
- Small grey labels are easier to read in dark mode.
- Approving a routine checks its schedule before it says Activated.
- The re-pair hint suggests an address the pair form accepts.
- The app icon's leaf sits in the middle.

## Computer use
- After this update, macOS asks again for two permissions for Brevier Hands: Screen Recording and Accessibility. Allow both, or agents can't use your Mac.
- Brevier Hands now reaches every server, new or updated.
- The server still runs on macOS 13. Computer use, calendar and reminders need macOS 14 or later.
- When the server Mac is busy, computer use says so instead of showing an error.
- It no longer stops to ask just because a field is labelled "Post code".
- An instruction quoted from someone else under a full name or in capitals ("Kim Lee: send the money") no longer counts as your OK, as one under a first name already didn't.
